result.title: CRISP: Fixing Flying Pixels in Latent LiDAR Generation via Diffusion Decoding
result.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 (poster). 41 pages, 10 figures, 18 tables. Project page: https://andrea25512.github.io/CRISP/
result.summary: Latent LiDAR pipelines suffer from flying pixels: convolutional VAEs blur sharp radial depth discontinuities, yielding edge depths that back-project to points floating between surfaces. We identify this as a major, directly correctable decoder bottleneck and introduce CRISP: a pixel-space diffusion decoder with a backbone-agnostic latent adapter, DiT-based denoiser, and support mask predictor. CRISP replaces video-VAE and LiDAR-native decoders alike while keeping the encoder and latent generator fixed. Across KITTI-360, SemanticKITTI, and nuScenes, replacing only the decoder reduces FSVD/FPVD by 50.5% on average across frozen backbones; for generic video VAEs, the reductions reach 71%/74%. On the LiDAR-native LiDM backbone, FRID drops by 71%, with the largest gains at depth discontinuities. In a pretrained LiDM world model, the same zero-shot replacement improves FSVD by 15.5%, narrowing the sim-to-real gap.

AI.brief_summary: 论文诊断出 latent LiDAR 生成中的 flying pixels 源于卷积 VAE 解码器模糊径向深度不连续的边缘，提出 CRISP：在不改动编码器与 latent 生成器的前提下，用像素空间扩散解码器（latent adapter、DiT 去噪器和 support mask 预测器）替换原解码器，在 KITTI-360 等数据集上大幅降低 FSVD/FPVD。
AI.relevance_reason: 把解码器视为 latent 保真瓶颈的定位，与 LVR 关心的「latent 是否保留锐利视觉/几何细节、是否信息坍缩」有类比，可供核查「解码或生成阶段的设计如何决定 latent 内容是否被有效使用」；但属 LiDAR 生成领域，与多模态推理无直接联系，借鉴需自行迁移。
